The Limitation Act, 1963 shall apply to arbitrations as it applies to proceedings in court, as provided under Section 43 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 [1]. An arbitration shall be deemed to have commenced on the date referred to in Section 21 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 [1].

For a suit for money payable for money lent, the limitation period is three years, and the period begins to run when the loan is made, according to Article 19 of the Limitation Act, 1963 [2]. When the lender has given a cheque for the money, the limitation period is three years starting from when the cheque is paid, under Article 20 of the Limitation Act, 1963 [4]. For money lent under an agreement that it shall be payable on demand, the limitation period is three years beginning when the loan is made, pursuant to Article 21 of the Limitation Act, 1963 [5].
